# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 6 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal Equivalent)

**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 6 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_006_page_001.jpg

---

## Vision 2, Chapter 2

**1** When she had finished speaking, she said to me, "Would you like me to read to you?" "Yes, my lady," I replied. "Then listen," she said. She opened the small book and read to me — not from the beginning, but from something in the middle of it, as follows: **2** "Behold, O God of Powers, who by your invisible and great might, and by your abundant wisdom, created the world — who by your glorious design clothed your creation with loveliness, and by your powerful word set the heavens in place and founded the earth upon the waters, and by your own wisdom and providence formed your holy church, which you also blessed — **3** Behold, he is removing the heavens and the mountains and the hills and the seas, and all things will be leveled for his chosen ones, that he may fulfill to them his promise with great glory and joy — if they keep the commandments of God which they received in great faith." **4** When she had finished reading, I stood up and said, "Lady, what does it mean that the heavens and the mountains and the hills and the seas will be removed?" She replied, "All these things, when they are removed, must serve the chosen of God in some capacity. For all these mountains and hills and seas and heavens are opposed to the elect and must be removed. Then those who are faithful and sincere of heart will enjoy good things, but the wicked will not enter in." **5** She said to me, "I want you to understand that it is I, and I alone, who am all these things: patience and love and truth, and the foundation and the building up and the protective wall and the tower and the power of the saints." I said, "Lady, explain this to me." She replied, "Do you not see before you the great tower being built upon the waters, with bright square-cut stones?"

---

*LOGOS note: "sincere of heart" for haplous — those who are pure/simple/undivided; complements "not double-minded."*
